questions.q: What was Jim's job while the others carried the gold to the boat?
choices: Packing the coins into bread-bags in the cave
Standing guard with a musket on top of the hill
Rowing the loaded boat out to the ship at anchor
Cooking the meals for everyone over the fire
questions.evidence: packing the minted money into bread-bags

questions.q: Why does Jim compare the coins to "autumn leaves"?
choices: There were so many of them
They were brown and crumbling
They blew away in the wind
They were found under the trees

questions.q: What did the doctor and Jim hear from the darkness on the third night?
choices: A noise between shrieking and singing from the mutineers
Ben Gunn calling for help from somewhere in the woods
The boom of cannon fire from another ship out at sea
The parrot screaming pieces of eight from the stockade
questions.evidence: a noise between shrieking and singing

questions.q: What did the doctor say he would do if he were sure the mutineers were raving with fever?
choices: Go and help them with his medical skill, at any risk
Shoot them from the top of the hill before they came near
Leave the island at once on the very next tide
Send Silver alone to fetch them back to the cave
questions.evidence: take them the assistance of my skill

questions.q: How did most of the group treat Silver after the treasure was found?
choices: Coldly, hardly better than a dog
Warmly, as a hero and a friend
Respectfully, as their new captain
As a prisoner kept in heavy chains
questions.evidence: none treated him better than a dog

questions.q: What was decided about the three surviving mutineers?
choices: To leave them on the island with supplies
To take them home to England to be hanged
To hunt them down in the woods and shoot them
To make them work as part of the ship's crew
questions.evidence: it was decided that we must desert them on the island

questions.q: What did the doctor especially want left for the marooned men?
choices: A handsome present of tobacco
The little goat-skin boat
A fair share of the gold
A new Bible to replace Dick's

questions.q: What did one of the marooned mutineers do as the ship sailed away?
choices: Fired a musket shot over Silver's head and through the sail
Jumped into the sea and swam after the ship for a long way
Waved goodbye from the beach and cheered the ship away
Set fire to the stockade so the smoke rose over the trees
questions.evidence: sent a shot whistling over Silver's head and through the main-sail

questions.q: Why did the HISPANIOLA sail first to a port in Spanish America instead of straight home?
choices: They were too short of men to make the voyage home
They wanted to sell part of the treasure there for cash
The captain needed a bigger ship to carry the gold
They had promised to let Silver go ashore there
questions.evidence: we could not risk the voyage home without fresh hands

questions.q: What had happened when Jim, the doctor and the squire returned to the ship at daybreak?
choices: Silver had escaped with a sack of coins
Ben Gunn had sailed off alone in the gig
All of the gold had been stolen from the hold
A band of pirates had captured the ship

questions.q: Why did Ben Gunn say he helped Silver escape?
choices: To save their lives
Because Silver paid him
They were old shipmates
To be rid of the parrot
questions.evidence: he had only done so to preserve our lives

questions.q: Ben Gunn "had connived at" Silver's escape. What does connived at mean here?
choices: Secretly allowed or helped
Tried very hard to stop
Slept right through it
Reported it to the captain
questions.evidence: The maroon had connived at his escape

questions.q: How many of the men who sailed out returned on the HISPANIOLA?
choices: Five
Seventy-five
Nineteen
Twelve
questions.evidence: Five men only of those who had sailed returned with her

questions.q: What did Ben Gunn do with his thousand pounds?
choices: Spent or lost it in nineteen days
Bought a fine ship of his own
Saved every penny in a bank
Gave it all to the village church
questions.evidence: in nineteen days, for he was back begging on the twentieth

questions.q: What became of Gray after the voyage?
choices: He studied, became mate and part owner of a ship, and married
He sailed back to Treasure Island to look for the bar silver
He spent all of his share on drink within a few weeks
He ran off to join Silver and became a pirate after all
questions.evidence: he is now mate and part owner of a fine full-rigged ship

questions.q: How does Jim feel about Treasure Island at the end of the story?
choices: He never wants to go back and still has bad dreams about it
He plans to sail back one day to dig up the bar silver
He misses the island and wishes he could live there again
He has forgotten all about it and never thinks of it now
questions.evidence: Oxen and wain-ropes would not bring me back again to that accursed island
